## The renderer

`output-constraint-renderer@1.0.0`, in `packages/opportunity-engine/python/sros_opportunity/output_constraints.py`. It reads the live output schema object and the explicit rendering policy; it never reads model output, execution history, a response artifact, any value an answer happened to have. Fields follow the schema's own required order and adjacent fields whose rendered lines are identical share a stanza. A note is guidance that is not a limit and may carry no digit, so every number the model reads comes from the schema.

| rule | class | why |
|---|---|---|
| `object_required` | A `MUST_BE_EXPLICIT_IN_PROMPT` | omitting a field fails validation, so the block states how many fields there are and that every one is required |
| `object_closed` | A `MUST_BE_EXPLICIT_IN_PROMPT` | a field outside the contract fails validation, so the block says no other field is allowed |
| `type` | B `PROVIDED_BY_TOOL_SCHEMA_AND_NOT_USEFUL_AS_PROSE` | the tool schema carries every field's JSON type, and the rendered wording (characters, elements, exactly one of) already presupposes it |
| `closed_choice` | A `MUST_BE_EXPLICIT_IN_PROMPT` | a closed choice whose selection carries meaning; the exact members are rendered |
| `composed_length` | A `MUST_BE_EXPLICIT_IN_PROMPT` | the model composes this text and has to control its length while writing it |
| `copied_length` | D `INTERNAL_VALIDATOR_ONLY` | the value is copied verbatim from what the packet supplies, so generation never chooses its length; the bound serves the capacity walker and the validator |
| `identity_grammar` | B `PROVIDED_BY_TOOL_SCHEMA_AND_NOT_USEFUL_AS_PROSE` | regex syntax is not useful prose: the block says which supplied values to copy verbatim, and the tool schema carries their canonical form |
| `annotation` | D `INTERNAL_VALIDATOR_ONLY` | an annotation the local validator does not assert; the pattern beside it does the work |
| `sentinel` | A `MUST_BE_EXPLICIT_IN_PROMPT` | the schema's own description names an exact string the answer must use when the field has no supported value; that is refusal behaviour, and it is rendered verbatim |
| `chosen_cardinality` | A `MUST_BE_EXPLICIT_IN_PROMPT` | the model chooses how many elements to write and can naturally write too many |
| `vocabulary_cardinality` | C `SEMANTICALLY_REDUNDANT_WITH_EXISTING_INSTRUCTION` | the items are drawn from a closed vocabulary no larger than this bound, and the vocabulary is rendered, so no duplicate-free answer can exceed it |

`WERE_OTHER_SCHEMA_BOUNDS_MISSING_FROM_PROMPT = true`. Besides `evidence_bound_reasoning_summary maxLength`, the bound V2 was refused on, v1.1.0 did not state:

- `subject maxLength 80`

- `recommended_next_evidence maxItems 8`
- `recommended_next_evidence[] maxLength 300`

Nor these generation-relevant constraints that are not bounds:

- `<root> required`
- `<root> additionalProperties`
- `target_actor_if_supported sentinel`
- `statement_classifications[] required`
- `statement_classifications[] additionalProperties`

v1.1.0 did state: `decision enum`, `supported_dimensions[] enum`, `unsupported_dimensions[] enum`, `critical_uncertainties[] maxLength`, `commercial_claims_supported[] maxLength`, `commercial_claims_not_supported[] maxLength`, `confidence_classification enum`, `statement_classifications[].classification enum`. v1.2.0 leaves 0 unstated.

Every array's maximum is stated unless the schema itself makes it non-binding: an array whose members are drawn from a closed vocabulary no larger than its maxItems cannot exceed it without a duplicate, and the vocabulary is stated. Identifier arrays are stated too, though this packet supplies fewer ids than their maximum, because that margin is a fact about one packet and not about the contract.

```
a_mutations                                        32
a_mutations_moving_the_prompt                      32

```

Every class-A constraint was mutated in a copy of the schema and moved the rendered prompt; every constraint of another class was mutated within its class and moved nothing; each vocabulary bound pushed below its vocabulary became binding and appeared; rewording every description left the prompt unchanged. Type keywords are not mutated, because changing a type turns the field into a different contract.

## The validator still decides

Local validator authoritative: `true`. `TRUNCATION`, `ITEM_DROPPING`, `REWRITING`, `AUTO_SUMMARY`, `STATEMENT_SPLITTING`, `SEMANTIC_NORMALISATION`: all `false`. The prompt communicates and the validator decides. An answer over a communicated bound is refused at stage 5 exactly as V2's was; nothing truncates, drops, rewrites, summarises, splits or normalises it to fit.
